utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Nice.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Your Honour, we dealt yesterday with the meeting with the accused in March of 1993, which was covered on the notes that the witness has been referring to, page 8 and the top of page 9. That being which tab of the exhibit? Three. Tab 3 of the exhibit. If we can go to the witness summary, there are a few matters that I just wish to tidy up about the meetings of which the witness has spoken. First paragraph, 98, on page 17.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Something I didn't ask you yesterday, Witness C-048, about the first meeting. When you saw Stanisic on that occasion, were you formally introduced?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-048 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, although I knew him previously. But Milan Popivoda [sic] introduced me to him once again, because Mr. Stanisic met various different people, so quite possibly he might have forgotten and not remembered my name. Milan Popivoda [sic] mentioned on that occasion to him once again that I was his man, and I quote that. He said, "Our man."

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: What, if anything, did Stanisic say when he was introduced to you formally or, rather, you were introduced to him formally?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-048 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The answer was, "Yes, yes. Fine. Very well."

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: As to Kertes, had you met Kertes before this meeting or not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-048 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Several times before that. He would come to the premises on his own.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Paragraph 113, page 19. Returning to the meeting with the accused, you tell us that you see where the group had come from, namely the regional board. The encounter or meeting in the casino, what was it like? Was it an official meeting or if not, describe it. How long did it last roughly?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-048 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The meeting itself was not an official meeting in the sense that there were minutes taken by a clerk and all the rest of it. So I would characterise it as being a sort of informal meeting, relaxation after an official meeting in the premises of the Regional Board, provincial board of the SPS. But they did discuss very concrete, specific, and serious issues.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Was it --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-048 [Resumed]
utterances.text: And those present were -- that is to say, the people I mentioned were present, those who made up the Backa Palanka lobby, and all the posts they held.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: No need to go over that again. Thank you. Was this in the same area of the restaurant as the previous two meetings or in a different area, or can't you remember?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-048 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was in the same part. And in addition to what I've already said, this was the part of the restaurant where they had Louis XIV-style furniture and it was the most exclusively furnished area.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Paragraph 125, page 20. In the course of this meeting what form of address was used by the accused to those with whom he was speaking? What form of address was used by them to him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-048 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The accused had a fairly familiar way of speaking to them. Of course he didn't use the "tu" form, the second person singular. But I must say quite frankly with the exception of Milorad Vucelic and Jovica Stanisic, they were fairly humble towards him. Whereas Vucelic Milorad and Jovica Stanisic would retain a sort of human integrity, if I can put it that way.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Did the accused know or use their first names, last names, or nicknames of any of these people or can't you remember?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-048 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course he knew the names and nicknames of all his associates. He would refer to some people by name. Other people didn't have nicknames. Milan Popivoda [sic], I never heard a nickname used for him at all. As for Kertes, he would say Bracika. As for Radovan Pankov, Rasa. Vucelic would be referred to as Milorad or Vucela, a combination of the two.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Paragraph 127, page 21. Just a few more things about the notes from which the notes in court were derived. The original notes, how soon after events did you write those notes down?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-048 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Two to three days at the most. I didn't do this the same day because sometimes I would have other things to do because I would be working for 16 hours a day in those times.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Just -- I know you've touched on this once already, but just again explain why you were writing these notes down, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-048 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I had no specific goal in mind. I kept my diary, and it was all very interesting for me, for an ordinary man who suddenly was involved in all these things. And of course I always have my logic in life. You never know what you might need something.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Turn briefly to the topic paragraph 128 or 129, Arkan and Arkan's Tigers. At paragraph 129. Did Milovan Popivoda tell you anything about his understanding of Arkan's position?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-048 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Milovan Popivoda said that Arkan's position he considered to be subordinate to the service. So somebody close to the service, in fact, and a man in whom the state security service had full trust and confidence in.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Did you hear any account of Arkan from anybody other than Milovan Popivoda?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-048 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did hear the accused at the meeting when he quite clearly spoke to Mihalj Kertes, with his nickname Bracika. And he said, "Bracika, are you and Frenki holding Arkan under your control? Do you have him under your control?"

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: My question may have not been clear. Was there anybody else of the people you've spoken about yesterday who told you things about Arkan or spoke about Arkan's position?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-048 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Milan Popivoda [sic] mostly and other people were mentioned. Veselin Vukotic, Darko Asanin, that the weapons and all the other things they needed, uniforms, medical supplies, and so on for Arkan's so-called Serbian Volunteer Guards should go via Frenki and that he was in charge of equipping them and procuring weapons and all the other materiel and resources that Arkan's guards needed. And --

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: You -- was there any Arkan's Tiger individual who came to work for the casino?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-048 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. After the Russian business partners in the summer of 1998 became partners in the casino and 70 per cent of that, Branko Bucalo provided security. And he had recommendations from my Russian business partners. And they said that up to then he had been in Arkan's volunteer guards and he had spent quite a lot of time at the fronts in Croatia and Bosnia-Herzegovina. Branko Bucalo was a very capable young man and was well able to perform his duties, and so I took him myself to be my personal bodyguard. And there were a lot of interesting things that we could talk about, so we became quite close. In fact, we became friends.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Did he tell you anything about, anything of particular interest about what he'd done as a member of Arkan's guards?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-048 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He told me quite a lot of interesting things. And what I found strange was that when he was 16, he joined Arkan's Serbian Volunteer Guards, because he was born in 1975, in fact. And he would tell me generally about what had come to pass in Croatia. And I clearly remember him mentioning to me that in the early autumn, that is to say in September, October, mostly September, I would say, when they went to Western Bosnia, the environs of Prijedor and Banja Luka, in order, as Branko Bucalo himself said, because he's not -- he's not a very good speaker, he's a very good guy, but he said that they were sent there to introduce some law and order. And he told me how they had come to cross the straight border between the international recognised SRY and the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, and he said that their commander, Commander Peja, as he called him, had paid an UNPROFOR -- bribed an UNPROFOR staff member and that he entered into a bus just for appearance's sake. And during that time, they held their weapons pointed downwards between their knees, between their legs. So he made a show of getting into the bus. And after that, they in fact did go to north-western Bosnia, that area. The location was Prijedor and Banja Luka, where they found complete anarchy. And even high-ranking officials of the Republika Srpska were in a state of panic because the situation on the ground had dramatically reversed to the advantage of the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Very well. And I think he'd also told you something about the methods of disciplining of soldiers or army members who weren't inclined to fight. Yes? If so, just in a sentence.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-048 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. They applied various methods to humiliate people, physically mistreat them and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Before I turn to one or two other topics and one or two or exhibits, I want you to try and paint the picture of communication between various parties as appeared from your experience at the casino. You've spoken of politicians and leaders, and you've spoken of criminals. Can you, in your own words, explain what nature of connection, if connection at all, there was between these different parts of the then-society?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-048 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Quite clearly a connection did exist. They would refer to each other with the second person singular. They wouldn't say it in the plural. And on Sundays, they would be at Milan Vucelic's house at Crvenka for lunch. And they would buy each other presents like the expensive watch I mentioned. Darko Asanin presented Milutin Popivoda with a jeep that had been stolen or a Fiat Punto vehicle, a car to his wife, his daughter, Milan Popivoda's daughter. And as privileges, as privileges, in seven and a half years, the financial police never came to visit our premises, so in my view, in my assessment, plus/minus 1 per cent, so I'm pretty sure, our tax evasions amounted to approximately 2 million German marks which we quite certainly wouldn't have been able to do without the support of the people I mentioned. They connection could also be seen in the personal solidarity between the people I mentioned that made up the Backa Palanka lobby and in that context when I say that when Milan Vucelic was replaced from his post as general director of Radio-television Serbia, for example, and that was in August 1995, his -- the person who replaced him, director of marketing in the television station when he was replaced, their friends from the same lobby helped them avoid being held criminally responsible and charges brought against them, because the true reason that Milorad Vucelic was replaced was financial abuse and not anything else.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Nice, it would be helpful, I think --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And not the conflict with the accused's wife.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: It would be helpful if we could get through this witness today. If you could bring the examination-in-chief to an end as soon as possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Certainly. Can the witness -- that concludes what I wanted to ask him on that last topic. Can the witness have, please, what is to become Exhibit 390, tab 17, signed sheets by him with annotations of the people he is able to recognise from the Kula camp video. I trust the Chamber has copies of these sheets.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes, we do.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: We'll just look at a few of them enlarged because they're new.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: But it's right, isn't it, Witness C-048, that you've signed these three sheets in recognition of your ability to recognise the people named there and on the basis described? Yes?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-048 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Perhaps we can simply look at the second sheet, 440. Enlarge that photograph. Who are these?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-048 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I apologise, but which one do you mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: On the --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-048 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The two final digits are 91, are they?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: On the screen. On the left?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-048 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. On the left we have Milorad Vucelic. And at that time, he just held a party function, and that was the vice-president of the SPS. He didn't have any state function at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: You've heard the learned Judge's observations about time. We need to move swiftly so confine your answers, if you would be so good. The next photograph -- Just look at the screen. On the left. This is 3716.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-048 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. On the left the person is Milan Popivoda [sic] and next to him is Franko Simatovic nicknamed Frenki.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: The following page, 4132.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-048 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is Stanisic Jovica, and Senta Milenkovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Thank you. And 2604.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-048 [Resumed]
utterances.text: First of all, somebody I don't know. Then the person who is in this hall and has been accused of war crimes. Then the person in uniform I do not know, unknown. The person behind Jovica Stanisic is Miodrag Zavisic, the head of the Novi Sad SUP at the time. Then we have Jovica Stanisic, Milorad Vucelic, and Franko Simatovic, Frenki.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Thank you. A few short topics and for the reasons just given as briefly as you can, did you see anything of Badza at Asanin's house or at Asanin's club at Dedinje in Belgrade?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-048 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did see him there.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: On the night of Badza's death, was he discussed by people in the casino? If so, who?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-048 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The same night they celebrated the birth of Vesko's daughter, and Milovan Popivoda was there as well as Milutin Popivoda, Milorad Vucelic, Asanin Darko and Veselin Vukotic and myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: What did they say about Badza who died?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-048 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They just said he'd died but they didn't comment on the reasons, on how he died. They were, of course, sad, and the celebrations were interrupted. Milorad Popivoda spoke of Badza as a patriot, as a man who played an important role in the organisation of the so-called Territorial Defence of Eastern Slavonia, Baranja and Western Srem. And they also said that he had coordinated operations on the ground, that is to say, the executive part, that he coordinated that with Arkan.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Were you able to assess from what you were told or what you observed, probably from what you were told, how Stanisic's authority compared with Badza's?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-048 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were personal friends. But I would say that Stanisic was more important, held the upper hand, especially as Jovica Stanisic was an intellectual, whereas Badza was a policeman in the classical sense of the word.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Another topic. Did you go to the Erdut centre from time to time with Simatovic and also on one occasion, I think, with Kertes and have meetings there with Hadzic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-048 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: And if you want to follow some direct quotations, this can be found on page 9 of 12 of tab 3, the notes. And Witness C-048, if you want to you can find these in the registry pages at the top right-hand corner, 6465. Can he have those notes. Did you go on an occasion in April 1993 with Asanin and Simatovic in Asanin's jeep?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-048 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Did you arrive at Erdut and did you see the staff of the president as he was known, Hadzic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-048 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... Turn to page 6465 in the notes so that you can deal with it in the most expeditious way possible. And when Frenki got out of the jeep, what was the reaction of the unit commander there at Erdut?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-048 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The commander of the unit that provided security for Goran Hadzic reported to him. So the commander of that unit, the unit commander providing security reported to him.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Following greetings, was there then a private conversation between Frenki and Hadzic for about an hour, after which you went back to Novi Sad, to Belgrade?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-048 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Did you get off in Novi Sad --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-048 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Did they speak about political issues on this journey generally, including discussing the Vance-Owen Plan and did Frenki say that they had problems? If so, what did he say about the problems?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-048 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Franko Simatovic did speak about the problems he was having with Radovan Karadzic, and he said about him -- he said, "Well, we gave him everything and now he's trying to play smart now. He doesn't want to listen to us." And in that context he praised Goran Hadzic. He said that he was -- always listened and that there was no chance that he would escape control like the other one. And the other one was clearly meant to mean Radovan Karadzic. And he would also say with respect to Goran Hadzic that he had been a warehouse clerk before that and that he was happy to hold the position he held now and that he had no plans of making any difficulties or meddling in any affairs.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Bottom of the page before I come to --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please, Mr. Nice.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: At the bottom of the page following a note that says "May 1993." Was there another trip to Goran Hadzic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-048 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Were Kertes, Asanin and yourself involved, and if so, just briefly looking at the note, what was said on this occasion?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-048 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The trip was the same. By that time, the Vance-Owen Peace Plan for Bosnia had already fallen through. Mihalj Kertes also spoke about the problems in communication with Milan Babic and that it was necessary to promote Goran Hadzic about whom he stressed that he was obedient and that this was an ideal post for him.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Tidying those matters up. From page 23, paragraphs 138 and on of the summary. On the first meeting at Erdut, whom, if anything, saluted who -- whom?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-048 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The commander of the unit first saluted Frenki Simatovic, which is in accordance with the rules of the service.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: On the way back again with this first trip, on the way back to Novi Sad was anything said about who gave instructions to Hadzic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-048 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Frenki Simatovic did not mention the specific name, but he said that he got instructions from us, meaning the Serbian state power, the state authorities.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Paragraph 141. Was there another occasion at Asanin's house when Frenki spoke about the RSK leadership? If so, what do you remember him saying?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-048 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He said in the same context that Goran Hadzic was obedient, that he listened to them. He mentioned Radovan Karadzic in the opposite context, and he clearly stated the sentence regarding the arming of Serbs in Croatia using the words, "We armed those people."

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Turning to the second meeting with Kertes and -- at Erdut. On the occasion of this visit when you went to see Hadzic, were there any forces or paramilitary forces present there that you could identify?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-048 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: What type of force?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-048 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The forces carrying out security matters, security of Goran Hadzic as well as of the facilities themselves.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: I should be directing your attention to the office of Hadzic. What forces were there at the office if you can recall?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-048 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Prosecutor, you mean around the office?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-048 [Resumed]
utterances.text: These were persons in uniforms, and they had caps of red colour, and they had the insignia of the special operations units comprising the four letters S in Cyrillic which look like the letters C in the Latin alphabet. And they also had red berets on their head.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Two final questions. Paragraph 143, dealing with the same meeting. On the return from the meeting, did Kertes say anything about the means or frequency of control of subordinates? If so, just what was it and explain it.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-048 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He said a sentence in the context that we have to keep reminding them who is responsible that they are in the posts that they are in at this time.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Finally, did Milovan Popivoda at any stage tell you anything that you can recall now about organisation of the Territorial Defence in the RSK?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-048 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Milovan Popivoda also said that these jobs were done by people from Serbia, primarily Frenki Simatovic and Mihalj Kertes who organised the distribution of weapons from warehouses of the TO in the Republic of Serbia and from the weapons which the JNA illegally seized from the Republic of Croatia following the democratic elections, and in cooperation with as they called it the patriotic elements of the JNA which they distributed to the Serbs in Croatia which used those weapons to begin a rebellion against the authorities in the Republic of Croatia.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Thank you. You will be asked further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. C-048, yesterday you said at the beginning of your testimony that you were ashamed. I didn't understand very well whether the company you were in or the company you kept or all of the things that you did yourself or one or the other. Could you please be so kind and explain this to me?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-048 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course. Your Honours, I am ashamed of everything that I did. Especially I am ashamed of spying on my two best friends. I'm ashamed that I participated in the organisation of the attack on the priest's mother, an old woman of 70 years old who had welcomed me numerous times in her home, and everything else that I did during those years. Also during those years as a young man - I have to admit that also - I did not think in the same way that I am thinking now, and I didn't realise who Veselin "Vesko" Vukotic and Darko Asanin and the other people really were. And I must admit that I looked upon Vesko Vukotic as my idol.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Very well. You said you were testifying here because you felt it was the duty of every honourable man. That is what you said.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-048 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Here, just like at any other court.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Very well. But it is not in dispute that people whom you mentioned, the priest, this Coban, this journalist who was your best friend were people who were very close to you; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-048 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And you accepted to spy on them for money; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-048 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not exclusively for money. I wouldn't say that. My salary at the casino was part of it. I didn't specifically receive money for that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Well, I thought that that is how I understood your explanation. You agreed to do that because you were paid to do so.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-048 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had a very good job, and I was thinking that there was a danger that I might lose that job and the comfortable and easy life I was enjoying should I reject this offer.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Could you please tell me whether there is anything else that you are ashamed of besides the things that you have told us?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: I don't think the witness need answer that. If you've got some particular point, you can put it.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I do, Mr. May. I do, unfortunately, or perhaps by luck.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-048 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember -- I cannot remember the numbers, but I'm quite sure that I did not commit any armed robbery.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Fairly obvious risk, once we start identifying documents that might be public, of identification. The accused is putting an identifiable document. I don't know how easy it will be for the public to deal with it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. We'll go into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Are we in open session again now?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, we're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Witness C-048, have we established that you were convicted to an unconditional term of prison --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: I've already told you that that matter is not a matter for you to raise now, any matter like that. Now, if you want to -- if you want to continue your cross-examination, you will do so under the instructions of the Trial Chamber. Now, move on to something else.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. May, are we in open session?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. May, I should like to protest, and I object to you -- my objection is to you, that you are not allowing, regardless of the fact that we're not disclosing the identity of the witness thereby, to bring into question the credibility of the witness. You're not allowing me to do that, a witness who is quite obviously lying.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: The mistake that you make is to think that matters have to be repeated over and over again and rulings challenged. Now, stop arguing and go on to something else if you want to ask the witness something else.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Of course I do want to ask the witness something else, and I'm very pleased that we were able to note that what I claimed was true and correct. That for itself speaks of who the opposite side over there is bringing in to testify into this courtroom.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. C-048, you were born -- you were the child of a mixed marriage. Your father was Serb. Your mother was a Croat; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-048 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: You can answer in Croatian too, I'll understand you. You don't have to answer in English.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-048 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Don't be cynical. You have been cynical and lied for 13 years so perhaps you could refrain from doing that now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Witness C-048, it may be provoking to listen to these questions, particularly the nature of some of them, but accused will be stopped if he is offensive or he uses oppressive tactics, so you need have no fear about that. But we'll get on more quickly if you simply answer the questions and answer them as shortly as you can. But would you remember, and also the accused, that you speak the same language and therefore there is a danger that not enough time is given to the interpreters to interpret questions and answers. So would you pause between the two.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I do apologise, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I understand that the witness is disturbed, Mr. May, because of the facts that we have just ascertained, he is upset.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: No. You restrain yourself from your comments, comments of that sort which do not assist anybody.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, it does assist. It probably assists those who want to understand the truth, that this behaviour falls into the context of the lives and times that the witness worked in and how he was given this judgement.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, please, when did you become a citizen of Croatia?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-048 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I became a citizen of Croatia at the beginning of April 1988.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-048 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, 1998. I do apologise. It wasn't possible in 1988. I do apologise, Your Honours, in 1998.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Right. 1998?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: I'm sorry. Could I just ask for a private session for one minute?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: I will say this to the public. Various passages have been redacted. They are not to be used in the circumstances in any public way or to be referred to or revealed. Yes, Mr. Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have a principled and a concrete objection. The principled objection --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: We will go into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Then I will not state my objection. I would like to bring out or state the objection in an open session. My objection, Mr. May --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Are we in private session?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Very well. We'll go into private session. If you're going to raise any matter, you can do it in private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So that we do not go back into private session again, Mr. May, are we clear on the fact that the place of employment of the witness and everything else that he talked about regarding the company where he worked was something that was stated in open session?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Nice, you can assist us on that. My recollection is yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So in your statement, you talk about some company called MP Royal.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-048 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's not some company, it's the company MP Royal.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. For me it's some company. There are thousands and thousands of company.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-048 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it's a legal company. This is what I'm thinking of.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Do you know that for years you worked in the company whose full name is not that? What is the full name of the company where you worked for many years?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-048 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, MP Royal was the name until mid-1998 when in accordance with the changes on law on enterprises the name of the company changed to Royal DO company with limited liability.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-048 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is when the law on enterprises was adopted and when this transformation was implemented and when we entered into business relations with Russian business partners. So for those reasons it wasn't MP Royal any more but Royal DO. But it was still the same legal entity.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Since I have here the register which as you know is a public document and in it states that this company, as I said, is Royal DO, and it's an export/import company, and so on and so forth, for trade organisation and for games of chance. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-048 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: You said that the owner was a certain Veselin Vukotic; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-048 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I said he was the actual and only owner until July or August of 1998.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: As you know, a public document is a document that would also contain the record or registry of ownership.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-048 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: I got this document from my associates. It was obtained by them. So under 1, Vukovic Lidija, father's name Ivo from Dusseldorf, Germany. Are you familiar with the name of this entity?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-048 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is the unmarried or common-law wife of Veselin "Vesko" Vukotic. And I just want to say that the name of her father is not Ivo but it is Radonja, that Ivo is probably the name of the street.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. You are probably right. Let's go on. Ivanovic Spasoje, Belgrade. Do you know him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-048 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course. He was also the formal owner who received the money very often during the first two years of work in October 1994, Spasoje officially left the enterprise. He was an acquaintance of Vukotic, and he was the domestic founder of the company, if you're thinking of the foundation documents from 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: No. I am only thinking about the founding documents that we're talking about here. And then under 3 it says Vukotic Veselin, Novi Sad. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-048 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Never at the same time in official documents were Spasoje Ivanovic and Veselin Vukotic mentioned at the same time. You are probably holding the document on the change of the founder from October 1994.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: I have this document, and I will submit it as an exhibit. Under 1 it is Vukovic Lidija. Under 2 it's Ivanovic Spasoje. Under 3, it's Veselin Vukotic and then it continues, Anatolij Luginom, some Russian, Vasilij Siricenko and so on. However, these are copies of the registry document -- registration document, and this has not been translated, but if necessary, I will hand it over to Mr. Tapuskovic to look at. This is a common kind of form, so we can then continue so that we do not waste time.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-048 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I would ask to look at the documents in order to give any kind of answer, because changes were made in such documents several times.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- So --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Before the witness sees the document, Mr. May --

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And since you -- Well, since you claim that you were the director of the company.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-048 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Nowhere here is your name entered into this registration document.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-048 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course not because the official director who would be subjected to criminal liability in case of tax evasion of a massive scale was discovered would be a third person. I would not place myself in such a position.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: You were the actual director in a company which was involved in crime and the responsibility was borne by someone else; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-048 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, the company was not involved in crime. The main activity were games of chance. Tax evasion at that time was something that was considered normal in Serbia at the time, as well as the state of the documents. I would like to repeat that under my management, the sum of about 2 million German marks was not paid, and there was never an investigation into our tax affairs because of the connections that the company had. The financial police for seven years that we worked never set foot on our premises.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Let him have a look at them.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As much as I can see, these are changes in the registration document from the 27th of December, 2002. Your Honours, is there any need to comment on this? This is a founding document from December 2002.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for the accused, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: You have 1992 there. Then you have these that I have cited here. It says that they are owners in 1992. Regardless of when we actually get the document, we can look at the most recent changes in ownership in a form, but there you will see all of the changes that happened throughout the history of the enterprise, and I'm saying that in all of those names your name is not mentioned as one of the directors of the company.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-048 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the -- also includes the original founding document. The found -- when the enterprise was founded, Lidija Vukotic was one of the owners, the common-law wife of Veselin Vukotic. She was the foreign investor of the company. It was essential that one of the persons in a company of games of chance would be a foreign citizen. Lidija Vukotic at that time was living abroad so that is why she was one of the founders. Besides that, the formal founder who didn't really have any connections, he was just a friend of Vesko's, his name -- his nickname was Paja Jajara. He left the firm in 1994. That was this other person. Veselin "Vesko" Vukotic in the beginning was not a formal founder because he committed a murder earlier. He killed Andrija Lakonic, and this was covered up by the secret service of Serbia. This was in late March 1990.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And then he appeared there in 1992.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-048 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He returned to Yugoslavia at the end of 1991 with the tacit permission of the service.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: According to the documents, we can see that he was the owner of the --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The speakers are going too fast.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Let's see if I have understood you perfectly. Although you were the main director, your name is not mentioned because you did not want to risk going into conflict with the law. So --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I note the remark of the interpreters.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Did you tell the investigator Tore Soldal this fact as well when you were explaining your activities?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Now, there must be a pause between question and answer not only for the interpreters but also that the microphone could be switched on and off. So could you both bear that in mind. Mr. Milosevic, do you want those registration documents exhibited? The company registration documents. Very well. We'll get the next Defence number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, Prosecutor's Exhibit Number?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Defence.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Defence Exhibit number 127.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Very well, Mr. C-048.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise, Your Honours. Should I answer the previous question? You put the previous question to me but I didn't give an answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. I interrupted, so would you explain the position to us, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Of course. I explained to the investigators and to the Prosecutors that the accounting books and actual state of affairs were different, but I possess the proper employment documents which state the actual number of years that I worked, and I have other documents proving my post as director in MP Royal, which I provided to the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: You didn't answer my question whether -- about -- regarding the facts due to which you failed to -- your explanation about why your identity was not included in the official documents about the founding of the company. Did you explain that fact to the investigators, to the other side?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-048 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I respect the other side very much. They are doing a very honourable job. Of course this is something that I explained that to them and they're aware of the real, actual situation and the bookkeeping situation, but I'm not quite clear specifically what you're asking me about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: That is a totally improper question and you know it. We'll adjourn now.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: With appropriate redaction of that question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. One more question like that and this cross-examination will stop. If you continue --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: -- You will not be allowed to go on cross-examining.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. May, as in my opinion you threatened to take my right away for cross-examination if I ask another question linked to the credibility of this witness, and I don't think you were right in doing so, may we move into private session for me to be able to ask another question in that regard?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Before you do, it is not questions linked to the credibility of this witness, as you know quite well, but a particular topic which has been ruled upon. But yes, let us go into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're now in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: You said a moment ago that Veselin Vukotic who was your boss, provided you with a job, was a sort of idol of yours. You looked up to him; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-048 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Is he from Novi Sad?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-048 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, he came to Novi Sad at the beginning of 1992 but he was born in Niksic where he lived until he was 25 and later on he lived in various places.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: You said that, to use your term, he was a man that one could trust and that people knew that he had liquidated Yugoslav emigres living abroad; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-048 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. That's what I learned about him before I actually came to know him.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Tell me when was that? When did he liquidate Yugoslav emigres abroad?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-048 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think you mean emigres from the former Yugoslavia who were ethnic Yugoslavs. I said Albanian emigres, not Yugoslav emigres.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: That's what you said.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-048 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I said Albanian emigres, the political adversaries of the former Yugoslav regime.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. And what was that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-048 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the mid-1980s and towards the end of the 1980s and the beginning of the 1990s, the killing in Brussels.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Would you have in mind the interpreters.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So are you claiming that that man was some kind of professional killer?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-048 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not only am I claiming that but in socialising with him, I saw that that was true. We became very good friends and he would tell me about the things he did.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. And he was your employer for many years; right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-048 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Now, this question of his activities, did you learn about those activities before you began working in his casino or after that, after you began working for him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-048 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The general things that were rumoured and talked about quite obviously I heard about those before I began working for him. However, the details that I testified about here, especially the details as to the killing of Enver Hadriu and Lakonic, I heard that personally from him.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please, to the accused. Microphone.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, but my question was did you know the person you were dealing with, the person that you described? And as you described, you knew about all this before you got a job with him and nonetheless you became an employee of his; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-048 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Now, you say that he engaged in the trafficking and the sale of drugs. Did you know about that too? Narcotics.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-048 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't say that. Your Honours, where does it say I said that? Could you look at the transcript or could the accused tell me where I said that he delved in drug trafficking?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So he didn't engage in drug trafficking?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-048 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, he didn't personally, but he had dealings with that kind of underworld.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Right. Fine. Now, as you say that this was a man you could trust, who could trust him? Whose confidence had he gained?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-048 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The security service, if that's what you mean. Or do you want me to state a name, the people who trusted him?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: You said that he was a man in whom one could place one's trust. That's what you said, isn't it? And as you say, he engaged in liquidations in the 1980s, as early on as the 1980s.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-048 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. So the state security service of the former Yugoslavia placed their trust in him, Stane Dolanc, Zdravko Mustac and others. And when the former state began to topple and the security system began to be dismantled, then he was a man that the state security of Serbia trusted.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: I'm not quite sure I'm following you. When you allegedly say you began working for the State Security Service of Serbia, he was not the one who gave you any instructions, was he? But as you say yourself, you received instructions from some sort of representatives of the State Security Service of Serbia, isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-048 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, my instructions were given by persons employed in the service.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: In his service?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-048 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In connection to the jobs I did for the service. No, I didn't get instructions from him.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So he wasn't working for the State Security Service of Serbia, was he? Is that right or not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-048 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He did work for it, but I didn't receive my assignments from him.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Well, what did he do for the State Security Service of Serbia? What was his job there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-048 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, specifically the liquidation of Enver Hadri in Brussels in February 1990 in front of the European parliament building. Enver Hadri.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And who was the head of the Serbian state security in February 1990? Can you tell me that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-048 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It wasn't Jovica Stanisic as far as I recall, but I may be wrong. I can confirm that. But Janackovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And somebody before him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-048 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mitrovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: What?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-048 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that the head of the federal service was Zdravko Mustac.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Zdravko Mustac was the head of the head of the federal service, was he? Zdravko Mustac was a cadre from Croatia; right?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: If you don't know something, Witness C-048, just say so. But if you do know, of course give the answer.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I'm trying to make a pause between question and answer so I give my answer once I see that the question has come up on the screen. So that is why I'm making pauses. It's no problem for me to answer straight away, but I'm bearing in mind the interpreters.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: You said that the chief of -- of the State Security Service of Serbia was Zdravko Mustac from Croatia; right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-048 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And a moment ago you mentioned Vukotic's activities during the sometime of Stane Dolanc is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-048 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Stane Dolanc was a leading Slovenian politician, was he not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-048 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of a communist Yugoslav orientation.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Without a doubt he was a leading Slovenian politician at the time. And he was the Minister of the Interior on a federal level; right? Federal interior Minister?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-048 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Well, do you then consider that he gave instructions and orders for those killings that took place in the 1980s that you mentioned?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-048 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was the individual who, in coordination with the other ministers of internal affairs in the different republics, would make decisions as to whether the ultimate solution would be applied to certain individuals, that is to say, liquidation of those individuals.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-048 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Veselin Vukotic told me that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: How would he know? How could he know? He was intimate with Stane Dolanc, was he?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-048 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't say he was intimate with Stane Dolanc, but as a man of trust he must have known about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: This man Vukotic that same year, according to you, in a Belgrade nightclub called Nana killed a certain person called Lakonic, and as far as I understood you, he was also a DB agent of some kind; right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-048 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, he wasn't also a DB agent. There are court documents and in the Serbian public there was an affair as to cooperation between the criminal elements of society and the state security service.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So you're saying that one DB agent killed another DB agent and not one criminal killing another criminal? Is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-048 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Andrija Lakonic was liquidated because he was a heroin drug addict and under the influence of drugs would brag in public about the things he had done for the service. It is true that both the victim and killer were criminals and long-term associates of the service.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So you say they were criminals and DB service members, agents?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-048 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Well, wouldn't it emerge from that that the service agents were criminals?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-048 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, when you say agent, I suppose you mean -- I take it to mean associates or collaborators, not working for the service full time.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So you mean that the service used certain individuals for their own purposes on certain occasions, is that it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-048 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, to do the -- its dirty work.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Well, tell me then, as you claim that you yourself were a collaborator or associate of the service, do you have any knowledge about how in a state security service somebody can give orders for somebody else to be killed? I assume you know the technology of how this is done. So explain it to us please so we can all understand.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-048 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course, Your Honours, I will explain that, although the accused knows full well how this works. There are never any written traces or evidence. A certain individual who was considered to be a threat to state interests, and when I say state interests, this was interests of a one-party system, they were people mostly of a democratic and liberal orientation of different ethnic backgrounds, and the decision in the former state was taken at the level of a collegiate. That is to say the ministers of the interiors of all the different republics and the federal minister as well. A team decision. And later the killing of Enver Hadri was the first one that was organised independently and autonomously by the state security of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. You're claiming that in the former Yugoslavia, in the Socialist Federal Republic of Yugoslavia, in fact when, it existed that a decision could be made at a meeting of the federal minister of his republican ministers to kill somebody. Is that what you're claiming?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-048 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Fine. Now, who gave instructions? Who gave the order? Because as you say, you cooperated very closely with Vukotic and Vukotic told you all about this. Who gave instructions in March 1990 for this killing, the killing that you're talking about? Who gave the order? You must know that, if you know that an order was given by the service as you say.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-048 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I know that the order was given by the service, and this I know from Vesko Vukotic, from what he said. And he said, "these people of mine told me to get rid of him because he talked a lot." That's what he said.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So who gave the order?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-048 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He didn't next that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Ah. He didn't mention a name. Right. Now, on page 3 of your statement, paragraph 2, you state the following. You say that: "He was never charged for the murder of Lakonic but an arrest warrant was issued for him, and he managed to escape, you say, because an inspector in the homicide squad in the Belgrade SUP, Miroslav Bizic was his name warned him and enabled him escape to Hungary. That's what you say in your statement; right? Border?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-048 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Up to the Hungarian border.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. Hungarian border, Hungary, it doesn't make much difference. But is that what you said in your statement?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-048 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But there was an error in the translation. I didn't say warned him but Inspector Miroslav Bizic helped him and brought him to the Hungarian border.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. Fine. Now, do you know that Miroslav Bizic was never an inspector of the homicide squad but that he was an inspector --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-048 [Resumed]
utterances.text: For adolescent delinquency?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: That's right, yes.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-048 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He worked in a different department, but Miroslav Bizic afterwards was suspended from service and he was held in detention for participating in the event.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. That's what you claim in your statement too.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-048 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It exists in legal documents too.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. A moment ago, I quoted paragraph 2 on page 3 of your statement where you say that Vukotic was never charged for Lakonic's murder. That's what you said, isn't it? Now, can you tell me this: You have studied law, you say. Explain how come Bizic was held responsible for being an associate, an accomplice whereas the other one wasn't charged with murder? Was he or wasn't he? Is what you say true and correct on page 3, paragraph 2? You say he was never charged for Lakonic's murder.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-048 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, there were certain mistakes made in the translation of my statement. He was accused and charged with some other individuals but was not convicted. And although he was -- made an attempt to flee, he was still prosecuted.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. Fine. Now, do you know that with respect -- that investigations were conducted against all the persons involved in the Nana nightclub incident and not only an investigation but Vukotic was accused of Lakonic's murder. He was charged with it. Do you know that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-048 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course I do. But nobody was convicted, and it turned out that Lakonic killed himself. That was the upshot. And Vukotic was freed of all responsibility and accountability, although he was a fugitive from justice the whole time. Others were in detention.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. And do you know that it was the district court in Belgrade, Judge Vladan Vukcevic was the judge in charge of the case when it was brought to court? You don't have to make such long pauses, you know. The transcript is always a little late. But the translation -- the interpretation is a little faster.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-048 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know the President of the Trial Chamber, by I know that there were legal proceedings.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Right. As legal proceedings were initiated, court proceedings, how then are you able to say such nonsensical things, that the DB tried to mask the murder and cover Vukotic if it was brought to court?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-048 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, this is not nonsense. It is the truth. They didn't try as to this cover-up. These people were acquitted of all responsibility and accountability, and Vukotic too, although he was a fugitive. And as I said a moment ago, it appears as if Andrija Lakonic killed himself.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Well, I don't know what it says in the judgement. I don't suppose it says that he killed himself.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-048 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it doesn't say that of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Well, we don't have to make a caricature of this, but tell me as you're a friend of Vukotic, is he living in Yugoslavia today?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-048 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. He lives abroad because there was a warrant out for his arrest for a killing in Montenegro on the 16th of November, 1997.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So you're saying he fled in 1997, did he?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-048 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, with my assistance.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: What did you say?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-048 [Resumed]
utterances.text: With my assistance.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Ah, with your assistance you say. Now, as since he fled with your assistance, do you have any contacts with him today, now?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-048 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not at the present time, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: What do you mean at present?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-048 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It means the last few years or perhaps -- a few months. Perhaps one year.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So until before a year ago you did have contacts with him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-048 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, more or less. I don't want you to hold me to the date.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. Tell me this: Did -- did you ask him what he thought about your appearing here as a witness? Did you ask his opinion?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-048 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not only did I not ask his opinion, he will probably ask that I be liquidated after my testimony here.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: What did you say he asked you? I didn't hear you properly. What did you say?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-048 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not only did I not ask permission from him to appear here to testify, but I think that he will ask that I be liquidated after my testimony here.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. Now, as you yourself said that after four weeks of work in the casino you became the boss for all the employees there; isn't that right? Then you carried out his orders directly, didn't you, his direct orders?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-048 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And that means that you enjoyed -- that he -- that you enjoyed his trust; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-048 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: In paragraph 4 on the same page, you say that in the beginning of 1993 MP Royal expanded and took over the Swedish gambling company, Cherry; is this correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-048 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Cherry.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Cherry?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-048 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that the owner of this company, a Swede, was also killed under very strange circumstances?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-048 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Do you have anything to do with this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-048 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. But Andrija Draskovic tell us when we took over the company and later on he became the boyfriend of the wife or the widow of the former owner.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Do you know who killed the chief of this company? As a person who enjoyed the confidence of this man who you say is a murderer, I would assume you would have to know this.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-048 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honour, I don't see why I would have to know this. The murder happened before we took over the company and it didn't happen in Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So you know nothing about this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-048 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't see why I should. His widow was -- inherited the company legally, and we concluded the contract with her.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: You say that the state security made use of your company, your casino, in order to gain control over certain people by letting them gamble, as you say, or supplying them with prostitutes. Is this correct? Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-048 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Can you give me the name of an individual over whom the state security service gained control in this manner? Because as an agent of the DB and the general manager of the company would have to know this.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-048 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I will tell you the name of one such person. Miodrag Mile Isakov, who is now the deputy prime minister of the Serbian government. He was then the representative of the independent journalists' association. He is a gambler, and he lost large sums of money. And during a certain period of time in early 1994, he gambled away the financial aid and the equipment that was granted him by the Soros foundation.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So the DB held this man Isakov under control in this way?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-048 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I told Milovan Popivoda about this, and of course I wasn't to know everything that happened. Mile Isakov gambled away the financial aid and the computers he had been given by the US embassy. No, I apologise, the Soros foundation from the Americans. And very soon after that an inspection arrived from the Soros foundation because of course people didn't want to squander money away on computers that would be gambled away by someone, and they asked Isakov to show them where the computers were.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters did not hear the accused.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Gained control over people whom they allowed to act in this way. So did it gain control over Isakov?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-048 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't see why I, as one of the collaborators of the DB, would have to know this, whether he was under their control or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: But I asked you to explain your claim that the DB used your company and the casino in order to gain control over certain people, and I asked you to name an individual and you named him. So my question is something that follows logically. Is this an example of the manner in which the DB gained control over this man? Did it gain control over him or not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-048 [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the context and the circumstances, it is my opinion that they did, yes. That's my opinion based on circumstances, but I cannot assert decidedly whether this was so or not. Only Milan Popivoda [sic] could confirm this.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: The service is responsible for Mile Isakov gambling, gambling away the Soros donation, the money he had been given? Is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-048 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, Your Honours, that's not what I'm saying. But the service, having this information, had this man under their control.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: You say that you started working for the DB in July 1992. This is on page 3, paragraph 7 of your statement.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-048 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But I corrected this. It was in June, not July. I made this correction when talking to the OTP earlier.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: How then do you explain what you say on this same page in paragraph 3 that for weeks after becoming employed there in 1993, you became the general manager of the company?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-048 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Do you mean the year?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-048 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's an error.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Another error?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-048 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It could be a translation error.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Very well. So yet another error. This cannot be explained then. You did not begin working for the DB before you got your job in the casino.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-048 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, I didn't. This must be a typing error.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: A typing error?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. May, may I ask him in public session how old he was at the time?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: How old were you then?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-048 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Twenty-two. Not yet. I was actually 21.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, since you say you were an agent of the DB, does that mean that you also had an official pass, an official identity card of the state security?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-048 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't. No collaborator was issued with identity papers. It was only people who were employed full time by the service.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Does that mean in fact that you were a spy of the DB or a police spy, an informer?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-048 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I was a collaborator of the state security service.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: A collaborator who was not employed by the DB, an external associate.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-048 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, there is a clear distinction between the employees of the DB who we might call agents and collaborators such as Veselin Vukotic and myself. I had a telephone for emergency cases, 6225542, and the extension was 021, and Popivoda used this phone if we needed to contact the DB urgently.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Very well. On page 3, in paragraph 7, you say that Milovan Popivoda was the head of the DB in Vojvodina. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-048 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: But that he was also in charge of Eastern Slavonia, Baranja, and Western Srem. Is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-048 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, I am saying that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So you are claiming that they did not have their own security service but that the Serbian Security Service operated in Eastern Slavonia, Baranja, and Western Srem, and that it was this Popivoda who was in charge.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-048 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They did have their own service, but formally, only formally. It was actually part of the DB of Serbia. It was financed from Serbia. Some of the staff came from Serbia and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Are you trying to say that Popivoda was -- that this was said to you by Popivoda, the head of the DB in Vojvodina, in confidence?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-048 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So he confided in you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-048 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I wouldn't call it confiding, but when he told me this, he never dreamt how all this would end and where I would end up.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Very well. On page 4 in paragraph 1, you say you don't want to justify your own actions but you try to do so by saying that you were against the plan to create a Greater Serbia. Is that what you said? Is that so?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-048 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Did the investigator Tore Soldal ask you whether you were against the plan to create a Greater Serbia or did you say this of your own initiative?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-048 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nobody asked me this. I said this on my own initiative.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Very well. As you said it, it was your idea to say this, when and how did you hear of a plan to create a Greater Serbia?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-048 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I would be pleased to answer this question. To the last questions put to me by Mr. Geoffrey Nice, I already explained where and how and under what circumstances I heard this, and I said to the best of my recollection in view of the passage of time when I had heard this, and I think this is sufficient if I have to expand on this.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Well, I can't remember everything you said exactly so I'm asking you again. From whom and where did you hear about the plan to create a Greater Serbia? Answer me in brief.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-048 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard you in Royal in early March 1993, among others.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: We'll come to that later. And I mentioned a Greater Serbia then?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-048 [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mentioned the creation of a single Serbian state.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Is that so? Well, we'll come to that. But now let's proceed according to your statement. On page 4, in paragraph 2 you say that you were told to monitor the Catholic priest Marko Kljajic, and Robert Coban, editor-in-chief of the newspaper, Nezavisni Svet. They were Croats who as you say were suspected of cooperating with both the Croatian -- with the Croatian intelligence services. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-048 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And that, you say, was your task?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-048 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not my alleged task it was my task.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: I say alleged because that's what you're claiming. I'm quoting you.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-048 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I am asserting it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
